subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff — autoscale, queues, embeddings pathways
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ng <alex.ng@novapay.com>, Sam Berger <sam.berger@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff — autoscale, queues, embeddings pathways

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side plus the small set of follow-ups that will help us size a Dedicated capacity recommendation and draft a short SOW: 

Recap (top-line)
- You’d like Redwood Dedicated to host model endpoints for customer-facing chat (low-latency) and a separate embeddings pipeline for semantic search + reranking.
- Data residency: us-east preferred; SAML SSO for console access.
- Retention and audit: ~30 days logs, SOC2-required evidence requested.

Immediate ask (so we can produce a sizing + autoscale proposal) — could you confirm the following: 
1) Expected steady-state and peak QPS for the chat endpoint (RPS or requests/sec), and typical burst pattern (duration of burst).
2) Average request size in tokens (prompt + expected response) and percent of requests that use tool-calling/structured output workflows (rough %).
3) Embeddings workload: documents count, updates cadence (real-time vs nightly), average vector dimension (if known), and whether embeddings/reranker must be realtime.
4) Any hard concurrency or latency SLOs (p95 target) for chat.
5) Are there compliance constraints we should model in the SOW (IP restrictions, export controls, split-tenant requirements)?

Attached is a short sizing worksheet (dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx) — if you can fill the highlighted rows (QPS, tokens per request, doc counts) it’ll let us produce a concrete autoscale proposal.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill worksheet -> we produce a draft SOW and a recommended autoscale policy (min/max GPUs, warm pools, burst capacity).
- Technical deep-dive with Diego (SE) to review auth (SAML, VPC peering), routing, and embedding batch design.

If convenient, we can lock a 30–45m deep-dive next week — suggested slots Tue/Wed morning (US ET).

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff — autoscale, queues, embeddings pathways

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Filling in the worksheet now, but quick answers below to unblock sizing: 

1) Traffic: steady-state ~150 req/s for the chat front-end, occasional marketing-driven bursts up to ~600 req/s lasting 10–20 minutes. Bursts are infrequent (2–3 times/week).

2) Tokens: average prompt ~550 tokens, expected model output ~700 tokens -> ~1.25k tokens total. ~18% of user sessions will trigger a tool call (we call an internal payments API) which will add ~1 round-trip of structured output (small).

3) Embeddings: ~2.1M documents now; index updates nightly (batch). We plan to reindex the full corpus weekly. Using 768-dim vectors; embeddings are used for candidate retrieval followed by an expensive reranker (cross-encoder) on the top 50 candidates. Reranker needs low-latency for the synchronous user flow.

4) SLOs: p95 latency for top-line chat should be <= 350ms; p99 < 700ms is desirable but not strictly enforced.

5) Compliance: standard fintech controls — data encryption at rest/in transit, SOC2 type II expected, 30-day telemetry retention. No export-controls beyond normal. On-prem is not required; VPC peering + private endpoints are preferred.

We can do Tue 11/17 10:00am ET for the deep-dive. Diego — looping you in for technical fit / auth details. I’ll upload a small sample CSV of documents to the Drive link if that helps.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform, NovaPay

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickoff — autoscale, queues, embeddings pathways

Alex / team —

Thanks for the data — that gives us a good baseline. From a Dedicated sizing and autoscale perspective, Diego and I sketched a recommendation below; we can refine on the deep-dive Tue.

Preliminary sizing (draft):
- Chat endpoints (latency-sensitive): provision a baseline of 4 GPUs in the Dedicated pool (quantized LLMs with optimized kernels). Target concurrency per GPU: ~40 concurrent requests (optimistic; will validate in perf tests).
- Autoscale policy: min 4 GPUs, target scale-up increments of +2 GPUs, max 22 GPUs for sustained high-traffic events. Burst policy: allow temporary burst to a pre-warmed spare pool of +8 GPUs for short 10–30 min bursts.
- Queueing model: use low-latency routing for interactive chat (prefer immediate routing), but when concurrency saturates, apply a small-queue backpressure (per-user token budget) and route long-running reranks/embedding reindexes to a separate batch queue with dedicated worker pool.
- Embeddings / Reranker: separate embedding fleet optimized for batching (higher throughput, lower concurrency). Since you reindex nightly and do synchronous reranks (top 50), we recommend a hybrid: dedicated embedding workers that handle nightly batch jobs + a smaller realtime reranker pool sized for p95 targets.

Operational notes / asks:
- We’ll need sample traces with token counts (a small traffic dump) to validate the 40 concurrency figure against your payloads.
- Diego will lead the auth/VPC design: SAML + VPC peering + private endpoints look straightforward, but we need your security contacts for SOC2 evidence exchange.
- We’ll draft an SOW (attached SOW-template.docx) and a simple runbook covering failover and graceful fallback to hosted models if capacity is exhausted.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Alex uploads the sample CSV and the completed sizing sheet to the Drive link.
2) Schedule deep-dive Tue 11/17 10:00am ET (confirmed).
3) Diego and I will produce a draft autoscale policy + SOW by 11/19.
